Docs.param: Per asset band indexes (coma separated indexes, e.g. "image|1,2,3" means use the bands 1, 2, and 3 from the asset named "image").
WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Return as soon as we scan N items (defaults to 10000).
Return as soon as we have N items per geometry (defaults to 100).
Return after N seconds to avoid long requests (defaults to 5).
Return as soon as the geometry is fully covered (defaults to True).
Skip any items that would show up completely under the previous items (defaults to True).
JSON query expression for filtering items.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected. If a feature has multiple temporal properties, it is the decision of the server whether only a single temporal property is used to determine the extent or all relevant temporal properties.
The name of a subdataset within the asset.
The index of a subdataset band within the asset.
Xarray indexing method to use for inexact matches.
Output format for the tile or image (e.g., png, jpeg, webp).
Coordinate Reference System of the input coords. Default to `epsg:4326`.
Image output size limit if width and height limits are not set.
Height in pixels for the output image.
Width in pixels for the output image.
comma (',') delimited Min,Max range. Can set multiple time for multiple bands.
Add mask to the output data.

Docs.param: Return as soon as we scan N items (defaults to 10000).
Return as soon as we have N items per geometry (defaults to 100).
Return after N seconds to avoid long requests (defaults to 5).
Return as soon as the geometry is fully covered (defaults to True).
Skip any items that would show up completely under the previous items (defaults to True).
JSON query expression for filtering items.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected. If a feature has multiple temporal properties, it is the decision of the server whether only a single temporal property is used to determine the extent or all relevant temporal properties.
The name of a subdataset within the asset.
The index of a subdataset band within the asset.
Xarray indexing method to use for inexact matches.
Per asset band indexes (coma separated indexes, e.g. "image|1,2,3" means use the bands 1, 2, and 3 from the asset named "image").
WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Coordinate Reference System of the input coords. Default to `epsg:4326`.
Docs.summary: Options for collection-level point query operations.

Docs.param: Per asset band indexes (coma separated indexes, e.g. "image|1,2,3" means use the bands 1, 2, and 3 from the asset named "image").
WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Return as soon as we scan N items (defaults to 10000).
Return as soon as we have N items per geometry (defaults to 100).
Return after N seconds to avoid long requests (defaults to 5).
Return as soon as the geometry is fully covered (defaults to True).
Skip any items that would show up completely under the previous items (defaults to True).
JSON query expression for filtering items.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected. If a feature has multiple temporal properties, it is the decision of the server whether only a single temporal property is used to determine the extent or all relevant temporal properties.
The name of a subdataset within the asset.
The index of a subdataset band within the asset.
Xarray indexing method to use for inexact matches.
Identifier selecting one of the TileMatrixSetId supported.
Identifier (Z) selecting one of the scales defined in the TileMatrixSet and representing the scaleDenominator the tile.
Column (X) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixHeight-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Row (Y) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixWidth-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Output format for the tile or image (e.g., png, jpeg, webp).
Numeric scale factor for the tile. Higher values produce larger tiles.
Buffer on each side of the given tile. It must be a multiple of `0.5`. Output tilesize will be expanded to `tilesize + 2 * buffer` (e.g 0.5 = 257x257, 1.0 = 258x258).
comma (',') delimited Min,Max range. Can set multiple time for multiple bands.
Add mask to the output data.
Padding to apply to each tile edge. Helps reduce resampling artefacts along edges. Defaults to `0`.

Docs.param: Per asset band indexes (coma separated indexes, e.g. "image|1,2,3" means use the bands 1, 2, and 3 from the asset named "image").
WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Return as soon as we scan N items (defaults to 10000).
Return as soon as we have N items per geometry (defaults to 100).
Return after N seconds to avoid long requests (defaults to 5).
Return as soon as the geometry is fully covered (defaults to True).
Skip any items that would show up completely under the previous items (defaults to True).
JSON query expression for filtering items.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected. If a feature has multiple temporal properties, it is the decision of the server whether only a single temporal property is used to determine the extent or all relevant temporal properties.
The name of a subdataset within the asset.
The index of a subdataset band within the asset.
Xarray indexing method to use for inexact matches.
Identifier selecting one of the TileMatrixSetId supported.
Identifier (Z) selecting one of the scales defined in the TileMatrixSet and representing the scaleDenominator the tile.
Column (X) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixHeight-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Row (Y) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixWidth-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Numeric scale factor for the tile. Higher values produce larger tiles.
Output format for the tile or image (e.g., png, jpeg, webp).
Buffer on each side of the given tile. It must be a multiple of `0.5`. Output tilesize will be expanded to `tilesize + 2 * buffer` (e.g 0.5 = 257x257, 1.0 = 258x258).
comma (',') delimited Min,Max range. Can set multiple time for multiple bands.
Add mask to the output data.
Padding to apply to each tile edge. Helps reduce resampling artefacts along edges. Defaults to `0`.

Docs.param: Per asset band indexes (coma separated indexes, e.g. "image|1,2,3" means use the bands 1, 2, and 3 from the asset named "image").
WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Return as soon as we scan N items (defaults to 10000).
Return as soon as we have N items per geometry (defaults to 100).
Return after N seconds to avoid long requests (defaults to 5).
Return as soon as the geometry is fully covered (defaults to True).
Skip any items that would show up completely under the previous items (defaults to True).
JSON query expression for filtering items.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected. If a feature has multiple temporal properties, it is the decision of the server whether only a single temporal property is used to determine the extent or all relevant temporal properties.
The name of a subdataset within the asset.
The index of a subdataset band within the asset.
Xarray indexing method to use for inexact matches.
Identifier (Z) selecting one of the scales defined in the TileMatrixSet and representing the scaleDenominator the tile.
Column (X) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixHeight-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Row (Y) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixWidth-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Output format for the tile or image (e.g., png, jpeg, webp).
Identifier selecting one of the TileMatrixSetId supported (default: 'WebMercatorQuad')
Numeric scale factor for the tile. Higher values produce larger tiles.
Buffer on each side of the given tile. It must be a multiple of `0.5`. Output tilesize will be expanded to `tilesize + 2 * buffer` (e.g 0.5 = 257x257, 1.0 = 258x258).
comma (',') delimited Min,Max range. Can set multiple time for multiple bands.
Add mask to the output data.
Padding to apply to each tile edge. Helps reduce resampling artefacts along edges. Defaults to `0`.

Return as soon as we scan N items (defaults to 10000).
Return as soon as we have N items per geometry (defaults to 100).

JSON query expression for filtering items.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"

Identifier selecting one of the TileMatrixSetId supported (default: 'WebMercatorQuad')

Numeric scale factor for the tile. Higher values produce larger tiles.
Buffer on each side of the given tile. It must be a multiple of `0.5`. Output tilesize will be expanded to `tilesize + 2 * buffer` (e.g 0.5 = 257x257, 1.0 = 258x258).
comma (',') delimited Min,Max range. Can set multiple time for multiple bands.

Defines the number of equal-width bins in the given range (10, by default). If bins is a sequence (comma `,` delimited values), it defines a monotonically increasing array of bin edges, including the rightmost edge, allowing for non-uniform bin widths. link: https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.histogram.html

WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Coordinate Reference System of the input coords. Default to `epsg:4326`.
Maximum dimension in pixels for the source data used to calculate statistics.
List of pixel categorical values for which to report counts.

Defines the number of equal-width bins in the given range (10, by default). If bins is a sequence (comma `,` delimited values), it defines a monotonically increasing array of bin edges, including the rightmost edge, allowing for non-uniform bin widths. link: https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.histogram.html

Comma `,` delimited range of the bins. The lower and upper range of the bins. If not provided, range is simply (a.min(), a.max()). Values outside the range are ignored. The first element of the range must be less than or equal to the second. range affects the automatic bin computation as well. link: https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.histogram.html
The name of a subdataset within the asset.
The index of a subdataset band within the asset.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected. If a feature has multiple temporal properties, it is the decision of the server whether only a single temporal property is used to determine the extent or all relevant temporal properties.
Xarray indexing method to use for inexact matches.

Docs.param: Per asset band indexes (coma separated indexes, e.g. "image|1,2,3" means use the bands 1, 2, and 3 from the asset named "image").
WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Return as soon as we scan N items (defaults to 10000).
Return as soon as we have N items per geometry (defaults to 100).
Return after N seconds to avoid long requests (defaults to 5).
Return as soon as the geometry is fully covered (defaults to True).
Skip any items that would show up completely under the previous items (defaults to True).
The name of a subdataset within the asset.
The index of a subdataset band within the asset.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected. If a feature has multiple temporal properties, it is the decision of the server whether only a single temporal property is used to determine the extent or all relevant temporal properties.
Xarray indexing method to use for inexact matches.
Identifier selecting one of the TileMatrixSetId supported.
Identifier (Z) selecting one of the scales defined in the TileMatrixSet and representing the scaleDenominator the tile.
Column (X) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixHeight-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Row (Y) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixWidth-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Numeric scale factor for the tile. Higher values produce larger tiles.
Output format for the tile or image (e.g., png, jpeg, webp).
Buffer on each side of the given tile. It must be a multiple of `0.5`. Output tilesize will be expanded to `tilesize + 2 * buffer` (e.g 0.5 = 257x257, 1.0 = 258x258).
comma (',') delimited Min,Max range. Can set multiple time for multiple bands.
Add mask to the output data.
Padding to apply to each tile edge. Helps reduce resampling artefacts along edges. Defaults to `0`.

WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Return as soon as we scan N items (defaults to 10000).
Return as soon as we have N items per geometry (defaults to 100).
Return after N seconds to avoid long requests (defaults to 5).
Return as soon as the geometry is fully covered (defaults to True).
Skip any items that would show up completely under the previous items (defaults to True).
The name of a subdataset within the asset.
The index of a subdataset band within the asset.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected. If a feature has multiple temporal properties, it is the decision of the server whether only a single temporal property is used to determine the extent or all relevant temporal properties.
Xarray indexing method to use for inexact matches.
Identifier selecting one of the TileMatrixSetId supported (default: 'WebMercatorQuad').
The format of the output tile image.
Tile scale factor affecting output size.
Padding to apply to each tile edge.
Buffer on each side of the given tile.
Add mask to the output data.

Docs.param: Per asset band indexes (coma separated indexes, e.g. "image|1,2,3" means use the bands 1, 2, and 3 from the asset named "image").
WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Return as soon as we scan N items (defaults to 10000).
Return as soon as we have N items per geometry (defaults to 100).
Return after N seconds to avoid long requests (defaults to 5).
Return as soon as the geometry is fully covered (defaults to True).
Skip any items that would show up completely under the previous items (defaults to True).
The name of a subdataset within the asset.
The index of a subdataset band within the asset.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected. If a feature has multiple temporal properties, it is the decision of the server whether only a single temporal property is used to determine the extent or all relevant temporal properties.
Xarray indexing method to use for inexact matches.
Identifier (Z) selecting one of the scales defined in the TileMatrixSet and representing the scaleDenominator the tile.
Column (X) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixHeight-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Row (Y) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixWidth-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Output format for the tile or image (e.g., png, jpeg, webp).
Identifier selecting one of the TileMatrixSetId supported (default: 'WebMercatorQuad').
Numeric scale factor for the tile. Higher values produce larger tiles.
Buffer on each side of the given tile. It must be a multiple of `0.5`. Output tilesize will be expanded to `tilesize + 2 * buffer` (e.g 0.5 = 257x257, 1.0 = 258x258).
comma (',') delimited Min,Max range. Can set multiple time for multiple bands.
Add mask to the output data.
Padding to apply to each tile edge. Helps reduce resampling artefacts along edges. Defaults to `0`.

Docs.param: Per asset band indexes (coma separated indexes, e.g. "image|1,2,3" means use the bands 1, 2, and 3 from the asset named "image").
WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Return as soon as we scan N items (defaults to 10000).
Return as soon as we have N items per geometry (defaults to 100).
Return after N seconds to avoid long requests (defaults to 5).
Return as soon as the geometry is fully covered (defaults to True).
Skip any items that would show up completely under the previous items (defaults to True).
The name of a subdataset within the asset.
The index of a subdataset band within the asset.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected. If a feature has multiple temporal properties, it is the decision of the server whether only a single temporal property is used to determine the extent or all relevant temporal properties.
Xarray indexing method to use for inexact matches.
Identifier (Z) selecting one of the scales defined in the TileMatrixSet and representing the scaleDenominator the tile.
Column (X) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixHeight-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Row (Y) index of the tile on the selected TileMatrix. It cannot exceed the MatrixWidth-1 for the selected TileMatrix.
Numeric scale factor for the tile. Higher values produce larger tiles.
Identifier selecting one of the TileMatrixSetId supported (default: 'WebMercatorQuad').
Output format for the tile or image (e.g., png, jpeg, webp).
Buffer on each side of the given tile. It must be a multiple of `0.5`. Output tilesize will be expanded to `tilesize + 2 * buffer` (e.g 0.5 = 257x257, 1.0 = 258x258).
comma (',') delimited Min,Max range. Can set multiple time for multiple bands.
Add mask to the output data.
Padding to apply to each tile edge. Helps reduce resampling artefacts along edges. Defaults to `0`.

WarpKernel resampling algorithm (only used when doing re-projection). Defaults to `nearest`.
Identifier selecting one of the TileMatrixSetId supported.

comma (',') delimited Min,Max range. Can set multiple time for multiple bands.

Either a date-time or an interval, open or closed. Date and time expressions adhere to RFC 3339. Open intervals are expressed using double-dots. Examples:
A date-time: "2018-02-12T23:20:50Z"
A closed interval: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/2018-03-18T12:31:12Z"
Open intervals: "2018-02-12T00:00:00Z/.." or "../2018-03-18T12:31:12Z" Only features that have a temporal property that intersects the value of `datetime` are selected.
